new_statements.quote: 2.3 Stress. In Waimiri Atroari, stress is not a contrastive feature. In bisyllabic words, stress falls on the final position syllable. Words with more than two syllables may possibly have primary and secondary stress. The length of the vowel influences the stress pattern. Syllables with long vowels and glottalized vowels are stressed. (1) kaá.pa 'garden' (2) ka.pá 'she/he talked' (3) my.dý 'house' (4) wu.ré 'fan' (5) ta.bé'e 'capybara' (6) ty.rý.ny 'any small bird'. There are a lot of questions that I was not able to answer in relation to the stress system in Waimiri Atroari. I need to do additional research.

new_statements.relation_note: The the published catalog (classification weight-sensitive (tentative), evidence open-text) already codes this language from Bruno 2010, LIAMES 10 sec. 2.3 p. 94, as non-contrastive stress with long/glottalized-vowel syllables stressed, otherwise final in disyllables, longer words unstated. The 2003 dissertation is the earlier source of that very passage: the 2010 article repeats it almost word for word with the same six examples. The dissertation adds one sentence ('The length of the vowel influences the stress pattern.') and an explicit admission that the stress system is unresolved, which supports the catalog's hedged, weight-sensitive coding; same placement, same weight clause, so 'agre…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive. A syllable containing a long vowel or a glottalized vowel is stressed (kaá.pa 'garden' vs ka.pá 'she/he talked'); when no such heavy syllable is present, disyllables are stressed on the final syllable (my.dý, wu.ré). For words of three or more syllables the author only says they 'may possibly' have primary and secondary stress and gives no placement rule (her examples ta.bé'e and ty.rý.ny show prominence on the second syllable, in ta.bé'e on the glottalized vowel). The author states explicitly that the stress system is unresolved and needs further research.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only the hedge 'Words with more than two syllables may possibly have primary and secondary stress'; no placement of secondary stress is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated beyond the weight clause (long and glottalized vowels attract stress, overriding final stress in disyllables); the author adds that many questions about the stress system remain unanswered.
new_statements.identity_note: The dissertation describes Waimiri Atroari as spoken in the Terra Indígena Waimiri Atroari (northern Amazonas / southern Roraima). Bruno distinguishes an Atroari dialect (Alalaú River villages) from a Waimiri dialect (the Samaúma group: Mynawa, Karebi Syna, Pardo, Arine; and Curiaú, Cacau, Mare), and says her data come from consultants of four villages and two speech communities (sec. 1.6, 'Types of Data'). The stress statement is not tied to either dialect.

tone.quote: Esta língua apresenta um caso típico de reduplicação prosodicamente determinada. Neste processo, observa-se que a reduplicação está condicionada ao número de moras: o reduplicante deve ser bimoraico. ... Quando as duas primeiras sílabas são leves, o reduplicante copia as duas primeiras sílabas da raiz verbal e prefixa-se à base ... Quando a primeira sílaba é pesada (CVC, CVV e VV), o reduplicante copia a primeira sílaba da raiz verbal e prefixa-se o material à base
tone.locator: pp. 84-86, sec. 2 'Dados: descrição e análise': 'caso típico.. bimoraico' p. 84, 'Quando as duas primeiras sílabas são leves..' p. 85, 'Quando a primeira sílaba é pesada (CVC, CVV e VV)..' p. 86; phoneme inventory in fn. 1 on p. 84, not p. 85
tone.translation: This language presents a typical case of prosodically determined reduplication. In this process, reduplication is conditioned by the number of moras: the reduplicant must be bimoraic. ... When the first two syllables are light, the reduplicant copies the first two syllables of the verb root and is prefixed to the base ... When the first syllable is heavy (CVC, CVV and VV), the reduplicant copies the first syllable of the verb root and the material is prefixed to the base
